name: WordPress & WooCommerce maintenance business
description: A one-person WordPress and WooCommerce maintenance business with 25 recurring US clients (founder-stated), running since 2021. Updates, backups, security, and the occasional one-off project. The founder says it runs at ~96% margin on ~12 hours a month with no employees, and claims $300K+ lifetime revenue including pre-Stripe billing (self-reported; Stripe only shows billing since June 2024). Not currently listed for sale, though the description reads like a sale pitch.

mentions.evidence: ~$3,612 MRR (−1.9% L30), 23 active subscriptions, ~$3,812 L30, ~$50,831 last 12 months, ~$120,876 all-time on Stripe, ~96% L30 profit margin. Revenue synced Oct 7, 2026 ~07:28 Warsaw (05:28 UTC). Note: another TrustMRR stealth profile carries the identical description with different numbers (~$2,827 MRR / 142 subs / ~$117,863 all-time): profile (https://trustmrr.com/startup/startup-7df5029028b9). mentions.indieAngle: For you specifically: a Next.js/Supabase "care plan" for small SaaS and agency-built sites (dependency bumps, Supabase/Stripe key rotation, uptime, backups) at $99–$199/mo. It's the same model with a more modern stack and fewer competitors.

whyItPrints: Care plans are the most boring recurring revenue in web work: clients pay monthly so their site never breaks, and the work is mostly automated. 23 subs at ~$157/mo average (my calculation).
